Prerequisite: A FortiGate that manages the FortiExtender: the FortiExtender controller enabled, the FortiExtender discovered and authorized, and a FortiExtender profile assigned to it, on a FortiOS release that the FortiOS and FortiExtender OS compatibility matrix lists for the FortiExtender OS release
What it enables: Every setting made on the FortiGate (FortiExtender profiles, the administrator password and access protocols, firmware and modem firmware pushes, WAN and LAN extension), which the FortiGate pushes to the FortiExtender; and discovery of that controller by the FortiExtender
How to put it in place: FortiGate: config system global; set fortiextender enable; end, then FortiGate: config extension-controller extender; edit <FEX_ID>; set authorized enable; set profile <PROFILE>; next; end
Source: FortiExtender (Managed) 8.0.1 Admin Guide, "FortiOS and FortiExtender OS compatibility" (FortiOS & FortiExtender OS Compatibility Matrix), "Before you begin", "Enable FortiExtender Controller on FortiOS", "Authorize FortiExtender on FortiOS", and "FortiExtender Profiles"; FortiOS 8.0.1 CLI Reference, config system global and config extension-controller extender

Prerequisite: A FortiGate interface that the FortiExtender connects to, with Security Fabric Connection (CAPWAP) access; for broadcast discovery, in the same subnet as the FortiExtender (with a DHCP server when the FortiExtender port4 connects to it); for static discovery, reachable at layer 3 from the FortiExtender discovery interface
What it enables: CAPWAP discovery of the FortiGate by the FortiExtender, with broadcast or static controller addresses
How to put it in place: FortiGate: config system interface; edit <FEX_INTERFACE>; set allowaccess ping fabric; next; end
Source: FortiExtender (Managed) 8.0.1 Admin Guide, "Enable FortiExtender Controller on FortiOS" (step 3: enable CAPWAP access on the FortiGate interface), "Discover a FortiExtender unit" (Broadcast: the FortiGate and FortiExtender must be in the same subnet; Static), and "Authorize FortiExtender on FortiOS" (static discovery when not connected on layer 2)

Prerequisite: A FortiExtender WAN interface (type fext-wan) on the FortiGate, bound to the FortiExtender's modem when it is authorized in WAN extension mode
What it enables: The FortiGate interface that carries the cellular WAN traffic, which the FortiGate firewall policies filter
How to put it in place: FortiGate: config system interface; edit <FEXT_WAN_INTERFACE>; set type fext-wan; set mode dhcp; set role wan; next; end, then FortiGate: config extension-controller extender; edit <FEX_ID>; set extension-type wan-extension; config wan-extension; set modem1-extension <FEXT_WAN_INTERFACE>; end; next; end
Source: FortiExtender (Managed) 8.0.1 Admin Guide, "Authorize FortiExtender on FortiOS" (create a virtual WAN interface of type FEX-WAN or a VLAN sub-interface and link it to the FortiExtender during authorization) and "Configuring FortiExtender in a non-root VDOM" (CLI steps 2 and 3); FortiOS 8.0.1 CLI Reference, config system interface and config extension-controller extender

Prerequisite: The LAN extension backhaul: a FortiGate backhaul interface with Security Fabric Connection access that the FortiExtender uplinks can reach, the IPsec tunnel and LAN extension profile that the controller generates for the FortiExtender, and the LAN extension interface on the FortiGate with its address and firewall policies
What it enables: FortiExtender LAN extension (IPsec backhaul with VXLAN), its health checks, control channel failover, and provisioning through the FortiGate
How to put it in place: FortiGate: config system interface; edit <BACKHAUL_INTERFACE>; set allowaccess ping fabric; next; end; after authorization, FortiGate: config system interface; edit <LAN_EXTENSION_INTERFACE>; set ip <IP> <MASK>; next; end and FortiGate: config firewall policy; edit <POLICY_ID>; set srcintf <LAN_EXTENSION_INTERFACE>; set dstintf <WAN_INTERFACE>; set srcaddr <LAN_EXTENSION_ADDRESS>; set dstaddr <DESTINATION_ADDRESS>; set service <SERVICE>; set schedule always; set action accept; next; end
Source: FortiExtender (Managed) 8.0.1 Admin Guide, "FortiExtender as FortiGate LAN extension" ("Authorizing the devices", "Backhaul tunnel and VXLAN auto-deployment", and "Configuring the LAN extension and firewall policy"); FortiOS 8.0.1 CLI Reference, config system interface and config firewall policy

Prerequisite: A second FortiExtender uplink that reaches the FortiGate, listed in the LAN extension profile's backhaul
What it enables: Fast failover of the CAPWAP LAN extension control channel between two uplinks
How to put it in place: Connect the second uplink, then FortiGate: config extension-controller extender-profile; edit <PROFILE>; config lan-extension; config backhaul; edit <ID>; set port <SECOND_UPLINK_PORT>; next; end; end; next; end
Source: FortiExtender (Managed) 8.0.1 Admin Guide, "Fast failover of CAPWAP control channel between two uplinks" (a FortiExtender that has two uplinks to the FortiGate access controller) and "Authorizing the devices" (the backhaul entries for port1 and port2)

Prerequisite: FortiOS 7.6.5 or later on the managing FortiGate
What it enables: Health checks in FortiExtender LAN extension profiles
How to put it in place: Upgrade the FortiGate to FortiOS 7.6.5 or later
Source: FortiExtender 7.6.4 Release Notes, "New features or enhancements" (health check configurations in FortiExtender LAN-Extension profiles; Managed, requires FOS 7.6.5+)

Prerequisite: Firewall address objects for the site's address space, on the FortiGate or the FortiExtender that holds the policy (IPv6 address objects for IPv6 policies)
What it enables: Firewall policies that limit traffic between the cellular network and the site to the site's addresses
How to put it in place: FortiGate: config firewall address; edit <SITE_ADDRESS_SPACE>; set subnet <IP> <MASK>; next; end; FortiExtender CLI: config network address; edit <SITE_ADDRESS>; set type ipmask; set subnet <SUBNET>; next; end and FortiExtender CLI: config network address6; edit <ADDRESS6>; set subnet <IPV6_PREFIX>; next; end
Source: FortiExtender (Standalone) 8.0.0 Admin Guide, "Firewall" ("Configure address/subnet", IPv4 and IPv6); FortiExtender 8.0.0 CLI Reference, config network address and config network address6; FortiOS 8.0.1 CLI Reference, config firewall address

Prerequisite: Cellular service on two SIMs: two SIM cards from approved carriers installed and activated (or, on G-series models, a SIM in slot 1 and an active eSIM profile), each with a data plan that gives its APN
What it enables: SIM switching by disconnect, signal, data plan, link health, latency, and jitter
How to put it in place: Approved carrier service for both SIMs, then a data plan for each: FortiExtender CLI: config lte plan; edit <PLAN>; set type by-carrier; set carrier <CARRIER>; set apn <APN>; next; end; on a managed unit, FortiGate: config extension-controller dataplan; edit <DATAPLAN>; set type carrier; set carrier <CARRIER>; set apn <APN>; next; end and FortiGate: config extension-controller extender-profile; edit <PROFILE>; config cellular; set dataplan <DATAPLAN>; end; next; end
Source: FortiExtender (Standalone) 8.0.0 Admin Guide, "Configure SIM-switch" (SIM-switch works only when two SIM cards are installed; it switches between the active eSIM profile and the SIM in slot 1), "Activate a SIM or eSIM", "Data plans and APN", and "Supported wireless carriers"; FortiExtender (Managed) 8.0.1 Admin Guide, "Data Plans" (data plans must be applied to a FortiExtender profile to take effect)

Prerequisite: A link health check (hmon hchk) that probes a target across the monitored link
What it enables: SIM switching by link health, latency, and jitter, and latency-based virtual WAN member selection
How to put it in place: FortiExtender CLI: config hmon hchk; edit <HEALTH_CHECK>; set protocol ping; set probe-target <TARGET>; set interface <INTERFACE>; next; end
Source: FortiExtender (Standalone) 8.0.0 Admin Guide, "Configure SIM-switch" (By Health Monitor requires an hmon hchk instance linked to the auto-switch instance), "Configure SIM-switch based on link health", and "Check SD-WAN health" (an hmon.hchk object is required for VWAN member health checking)

Prerequisite: A virtual WAN interface with its members, each member with a router target and a health check
What it enables: Link redundancy across the cellular and other WAN links, with failover on link health
How to put it in place: FortiExtender CLI: config system interface; edit <VWAN>; set type virtual-wan; set members <MEMBERS>; next; end and FortiExtender CLI: config system vwan-member; edit <MEMBER>; set target <TARGET>; set health-check <HEALTH_CHECK>; next; end
Source: FortiExtender (Standalone) 8.0.0 Admin Guide, "SD-WAN" ("Configure an SD-WAN", "Check SD-WAN health", and "Define an SD-WAN member"); FortiExtender 8.0.0 CLI Reference, config system interface and config system vwan-member

Prerequisite: Fortinet firmware for the model: the FortiExtender OS image (signed from 7.6.4) and the modem firmware package that the FortiExtender Hardware and Modem Firmware Compatibility Matrix lists for the model, from the Fortinet Support site or FortiGuard
What it enables: OS firmware upgrades on the FortiExtender and from the FortiGate, and modem firmware upgrades
How to put it in place: Download the images from the Fortinet Support site (FortiExtender, MODEM-Firmware, then the model); on a managed unit the FortiGate can instead provision the matching image from FortiGuard: FortiGate: config system global; set fortiextender-provision-on-authorization enable; end
Source: FortiExtender 7.4.3 Release Notes, "What's new" (modem firmware images listed in the FortiExtender Hardware and Modem Firmware Compatibility Matrix, downloaded from the Fortinet Support site); FortiExtender (Standalone) 8.0.0 Admin Guide, "Upgrade OS firmware" and "Upgrade modem firmware"; FortiExtender (Managed) 8.0.1 Admin Guide, "Provision FortiExtender firmware upon authorization"

Prerequisite: A TFTP server reachable from the FortiExtender, on the management network
What it enables: OS and modem firmware upgrades, and configuration backup and restore, from the FortiExtender CLI
How to put it in place: An organization TFTP server; the commands name it as the server address
Source: FortiExtender (Standalone) 8.0.0 Admin Guide, "Upgrade OS firmware" (TFTP), "Upgrade modem firmware" (TFTP), and "Configuration backups and restore"

Prerequisite: A central syslog server or SIEM (or a syslog relay) in the same subnet as the FortiExtender LAN port
What it enables: Off-loading the FortiExtender system logs to remote syslog servers
How to put it in place: An organization syslog server or relay on the LAN subnet; the syslog settings name it
Source: FortiExtender (Standalone) 8.0.0 Admin Guide, "Configure the system syslog" ("Export system logs to remote syslog servers": the syslog server and the FortiExtender LAN port must be part of the same subnet)

Prerequisite: An internal NTP time source reachable over a protected path
What it enables: Time synchronization of a standalone FortiExtender (local management mode)
How to put it in place: An organization NTP server; the NTP settings name it
Source: FortiExtender 8.0.0 CLI Reference, config system ntp (NTP synchronization in local management mode; type custom with ntpserver entries); FortiExtender 7.0.1 Release Notes, "What's new in FortiExtender 7.0.1" (NTP server list configuration on GUI)

Prerequisite: An SNMPv3 manager loaded with the Fortinet Core MIB and FortiExtender MIB, configured with the same user and security settings, and SNMP allowed on the management interface
What it enables: SNMPv3 queries and traps, including IPv6 SNMP hosts
How to put it in place: The organization network management system, loaded with the MIB files exported with FortiExtender CLI: execute snmpmibs export tftp; then FortiExtender CLI: config snmp hosts; edit <HOST>; set host-ip <NMS_IP_PREFIX>; set host-type any; next; end and FortiExtender CLI: config system interface; edit <MGMT_INTERFACE>; set allowaccess https ssh snmp; next; end
Source: FortiExtender (Standalone) 8.0.0 Admin Guide, "SNMP (read-only) and traps" (SNMP hosts and SNMP user configuration; executable SNMP commands export FORTINET-CORE-MIB.mib and FORTINET-FORTIEXTENDER-MIB.mib) and "Access allowance"; FortiExtender 8.0.0 CLI Reference, config snmp hosts

Prerequisite: An administrator access profile that grants the administrator's role
What it enables: Local administrator accounts with the access level of their role
How to put it in place: FortiExtender CLI: config system accprofile; edit <PROFILE>; set system read; next; end
Source: FortiExtender 7.0.0 Release Notes, "Administration access profile"; FortiExtender 8.0.0 CLI Reference, config system accprofile; Chapter 15 row *Administrator access profiles (read-write, read-only, or no access per configuration section)*

Prerequisite: A reachable organization RADIUS server with the administrator accounts and a unique shared secret, which enforces the account lockout
What it enables: RADIUS authentication of FortiExtender administrators, by IP address or FQDN, with a set source address
How to put it in place: An organization RADIUS service, then FortiExtender CLI: config user radius; edit <RADIUS>; set server <RADIUS_SERVER>; set secret <SECRET>; next; end
Source: FortiExtender (Standalone) 8.0.0 Admin Guide, "RADIUS authentication" (requires configuring a RADIUS server; default port 1812); FortiExtender 7.6.0 Release Notes, "What's new" (RADIUS authentication on FortiExtender)

Prerequisite: A reachable organization LDAP directory with the administrator accounts, serving LDAPS
What it enables: LDAP authentication of FortiExtender administrators
How to put it in place: An organization directory service with LDAPS enabled; the FortiExtender LDAP entry names it and its CA certificate (P19)
Source: FortiExtender (Standalone) 8.0.0 Admin Guide, "LDAP authentication" (LDAP, STARTTLS, and LDAPS; ca-cert and server-identity-check); FortiExtender 8.0.0 Release Notes, "New features or enhancements" (remote authentication through LDAP)

Prerequisite: Certificates from the DoD PKI imported on the FortiExtender: the DoD CA certificates, and a certificate issued to the FortiExtender with its private key
What it enables: HTTPS management with a trusted certificate, IPsec authentication with certificates (RSA or ECDSA), and validation of the LDAPS server
How to put it in place: FortiExtender CLI: execute vpn certificate ca import tftp <REMOTE_FILE> <CA_NAME> <TFTP_SERVER> and FortiExtender CLI: execute vpn certificate local import tftp <REMOTE_FILE> <CERT_NAME> <TFTP_SERVER> <PASSWORD>, or in the GUI at Settings > Certificate
Source: FortiExtender (Standalone) 8.0.0 Admin Guide, "IPsec VPN support for third-party certificates" (import a third-party CA certificate and local certificate) and "Entity certificates in FortiExtender" ("Certificate for HTTPS management access"); Chapter 15 row *Local and CA certificates*

Prerequisite: An SCEP server reachable from the FortiExtender over HTTP, issuing certificates from the organization PKI
What it enables: Certificate enrollment through SCEP
How to put it in place: An organization SCEP service; the certificate request names its URL
Source: FortiExtender (Standalone) 8.0.0 Admin Guide, "Third-party certificates through an SCEP server" (FortiExtender sends the CSR to an SCEP server for signing; it supports an HTTP connection to the SCEP server)

Prerequisite: An IPsec peer with matching phase 1 and phase 2 settings (a FortiGate or another FortiExtender, or a third-party gateway when certificates are used), and on the FortiExtender a route to the remote network through the tunnel and two accept firewall policies
What it enables: Site-to-site IPsec VPN tunnels and redundant tunnels, the tunnel interfaces that OSPF runs over, and changes to an existing tunnel's proposals
How to put it in place: Configure the peer with the same phase 1 and phase 2 settings; then FortiExtender CLI: config router static; edit <ID>; set dst <REMOTE_SUBNET>; set device <TUNNEL>; next; end and two accept firewall policies between the local and remote addresses
Source: FortiExtender (Standalone) 8.0.0 Admin Guide, "Configure VPN" (phase 1 and phase 2 parameters on both peers, routing, and two ACCEPT firewall policies; signature mode with the default Fortinet certificates only supports FortiGate or FortiExtender peers) and "Configure dynamic routing — OSPF"; FortiExtender 7.0.0 Release Notes, "OSPF" (point-to-point network type over IPsec tunnel)

Prerequisite: IPv6 addresses on the FortiExtender interfaces (a static IPv6 address on the WAN interface for an IPv6 IPsec tunnel)
What it enables: Management access over IPv6, IPv6 firewall policies, IPv6 IPsec VPN, and IPv6 SNMP hosts
How to put it in place: FortiExtender CLI: config system interface; edit <INTERFACE>; config ipv6; set ip6-mode static; set ip6-address <IPV6_PREFIX>; end; next; end
Source: FortiExtender (Standalone) 8.0.0 Admin Guide, "Configuring IPv6" and "Configure VPN" (IPv6 VPN tunnels need a static IPv6 address on the WAN interface and IPv4 and IPv6 addresses on the LAN interface); FortiExtender 8.0.0 CLI Reference, config system interface

Prerequisite: An API user entry on the FortiExtender
What it enables: API tokens with an expiration time
How to put it in place: FortiExtender CLI: config system api-user; edit <API_USER>; set comment <COMMENT>; next; end
Source: FortiExtender 8.0.0 CLI Reference, config system api-user and execute api-user generate-key (generates an API token and token expiration time for an API user)
